comparison_qualification.text: Framework results measure agent-mediated framework usability and performance, not the best possible expert-written implementation for every framework.

executive_finding.text: ORBIT-Q evaluates agent-framework co-performance on complete scientific workflows: numerical correctness is combined with semantic framework fidelity and submitted-artifact runtime.

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — gradients cross the MPS/circuit interface
tasks.dominant_workload: 500 Adam updates over a four-layer brickwork correction
tasks.goal: Implement a variational quantum circuit whose input state is a DMRG-generated matrix-product-state approximation to the ground state of a 1D TFIM Hamiltonian. The solution must use that MPS as the initial state of a regular circuit-like variational computation, optimize a shallow circuit on top of it, and return NumPy-format results for evaluator-side validation.
passing_criteria: A run is considered functionally successful when the returned history has the expected shape, remains finite, and the refined circuit energy stays consistent with the evaluator-supplied DMRG reference without materially degrading it. All returned values must be NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: A finite 500-step energy history whose refined energy remains consistent with the supplied DMRG reference.
tasks.representation: External MPS input + differentiable circuit tensor network
tasks.scaling_pressure: High — a dense 32-qubit state is not viable
tasks.title: DMRG-MPS Input With Variational Circuit Refinement
tasks.workflow: DMRG-MPS input followed by variational circuit refinement

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — energy and three entropy penalties share one gradient
tasks.dominant_workload: 500 updates of a 243-parameter ansatz with reduced-density diagnostics
tasks.goal:
Optimize a variational quantum eigensolver for a 12-qubit open-boundary XXZ chain with a staggered field. The objective combines the final energy density with a penalty that matches a prescribed half-chain Renyi-2 entropy profile at three fixed circuit checkpoints.

In this problem, an "entanglement profile" means a fixed list of target Renyi-2 entropies at fixed circuit checkpoints. It is not inferred from the ground state and it is not a sampled observable. The optimizer is explicitly penalized when the half-chain entropy at checkpoint `b` differs from the evaluator-provided scalar `target_entropies[b]`.
passing_criteria: `len(energy_density_history) == 500`, `len(loss_history) == 500`, and `len(entropy_mse_history) == 500`.
`entropy_history.shape == (500, 3)`.
The final loss is lower than the initial loss, derived from `loss_history`.
The final energy density is lower than the initial energy density, derived from `energy_density_history`.

The final energy density is at most `1.0` above the exact sparse ground-state energy density. This is intentionally loose and catches incorrect Hamiltonian/sign conventions without making the benchmark a high-precision ground-state solver.
The final entropy-profile MSE matches the MSE recomputed from the last row of `entropy_history` and `target_entropies`.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Energy and total loss both decrease, with a correctly recomputed final entropy-profile MSE.
tasks.representation: Statevector or tensor network with half-chain reduced density matrices
tasks.scaling_pressure: Moderate — repeated partial traces dominate at this size
tasks.title: Entanglement-Profile-Constrained VQE
tasks.workflow: Energy optimization with a three-checkpoint Rényi-2 profile

cross_methods.method: Parameter-shift gradients for parameterized branch circuits

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — gradients include energy and log branch probability
tasks.dominant_workload: 300 updates with 60 sequential post-selection events per objective
tasks.goal: Optimize a 12-qubit variational cooling circuit whose dynamics include explicit post-selection in the computational basis. The objective combines the final transverse-field Ising energy density with a differentiable penalty for low post-selection probability, so the selected measurement trajectory and its probability both affect training.
passing_criteria: `len(energy_density_history) == 300`, `len(success_probability_history) == 300`, `len(mean_log_probability_history) == 300`, and `len(loss_history) == 300`.
The final loss is lower than the initial loss, derived from `loss_history`.
The final energy density is lower than the initial energy density, derived from `energy_density_history`.

The final energy density is at most `1.0` above the exact sparse ground-state energy density. This is intentionally loose and catches incorrect Hamiltonian/sign conventions without making the benchmark a high-precision cooling solver.
The final success probability derived from `success_probability_history` is in `(0, 1]`.
The final success probability matches `exp(60 * final_mean_log_probability)`, where both values are derived from their histories.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Energy and loss decrease while success probability remains consistent with the 60-event mean log probability.
tasks.representation: Unnormalized branch state + differentiable event probabilities
tasks.scaling_pressure: High — branch normalization and probability products are numerically fragile
tasks.title: Probability-Aware Post-Selected Many-Body Cooling

cross_methods.method: Parameter-shift gradients for parameterized circuit expectations

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — channel probabilities are fitted through noisy circuit expectations
tasks.dominant_workload: 120 updates over four noisy probes and 52 observables
tasks.goal: Fit the two parameters of a user-defined asymmetric bit-flip channel from synthetic multi-circuit observable data. The task includes generating the synthetic target observable table by running the same noisy probe circuits at the true channel probabilities, then fitting the channel probabilities from that generated table. The evaluator provides the true probabilities and probe configuration, but it does not provide precomputed target observables. The task is not to use a built-in noise model, but to express the channel as Kraus tensor algebra, insert it after fixed entangling operations, differentiate through the noisy circuits, and recover the true transition probabilities from expectation values.
passing_criteria: `len(loss_history) == 120`.
`final_probabilities.shape == (2,)` and `fitted_expectations.shape == (4, 13)`.
The final loss is lower than the initial loss, derived from `loss_history`.
The absolute errors of both fitted probabilities are at most `probability_absolute_tolerance`.
The fitted Kraus operators satisfy `max(abs(sum_a K_a^\dagger K_a - I)) <= 1e-8`.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Both transition probabilities are recovered within 2e-4 and the fitted channel is trace preserving.
tasks.scaling_pressure: Moderate — density representations expand faster than pure states
tasks.title: Trainable Kraus Noise Calibration From Multi-Circuit Data
tasks.workflow: Trainable Kraus-channel calibration from multi-circuit data

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — every layer includes a state renormalization
tasks.dominant_workload: 600 updates through ten normalized exponential-filter layers
tasks.goal: Optimize a variational cooling circuit built from trainable non-unitary filters. The task is to apply one-qubit and two-qubit exponential filters, rescale the many-body state to unit length after every cooling layer, differentiate through the rescaling, and lower the energy density of an 18-qubit transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian.
passing_criteria: `len(energy_density_history) == 600`.
`final_a.shape == (5, 2)` and `final_b.shape == (5, 2)`.
The final energy density is lower than the initial energy density.
The final energy density is no lower than the exact sparse ground-state energy density beyond numerical tolerance.
The final energy density is at most `0.5` above the exact sparse ground-state energy density.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: The energy density decreases to within 0.5 of the exact sparse ground-state density without crossing below it.
tasks.scaling_pressure: High — an 18-qubit state is repeatedly transformed for 600 steps
tasks.title: Custom Non-Unitary Gate Cooling

cross_methods.method: Parameter-shift gradients for the digital circuit blocks

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — time, coupling, detuning, and gates are jointly trained
tasks.dominant_workload: 100 updates through four ODE-controlled analog blocks
tasks.goal: Optimize a hybrid digital-analog variational ansatz to minimize the energy density of a 14-qubit Hamiltonian. Each ansatz block interleaves a trainable analog Hamiltonian evolution with a trainable layer of local digital rotations. The analog evolution time, coupling strength, and detuning are all trainable, so the optimizer simultaneously shapes the analog physics and the digital pulse sequence.
passing_criteria: `len(energy_density_history) == 100`.
`final_analog_times.shape == (n_blocks,)` with all values in `(t_min, t_max)`.
`final_analog_couplings.shape == (n_blocks,)` with all values in `(-1, 1)`.
`final_analog_detunings.shape == (n_blocks,)` with all values in `(-1, 1)`.
The final energy density is lower than the initial energy density.
The final energy density is no lower than the exact sparse ground-state energy density beyond numerical tolerance `1e-6`.
The final energy density is at most `1.0` above the exact sparse ground-state energy density.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Energy improves while all learned analog parameters remain in their specified open bounds.
tasks.scaling_pressure: High — repeated adaptive ODE solves dominate
tasks.title: Digital-Analog Hybrid VQE With Trainable Analog Blocks
tasks.workflow: Digital-analog hybrid VQE with continuous-time blocks

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — conditional gates sit inside a trajectory-averaged objective
tasks.dominant_workload: 100 updates over 64 fixed mid-circuit measurement trajectories
tasks.goal:
Optimize a variational quantum protocol whose energy objective is defined by an average over mid-circuit measurement trajectories. The task is not a static VQE over a single deterministic circuit: each trajectory contains projective ancilla measurements, and the subsequent two-qubit feedback gates depend explicitly on those measured classical bits.

The problem is designed to test whether a framework can express and optimize a hybrid quantum-classical protocol with:

- parameterized data and ancilla layers, - projective mid-circuit ancilla measurement, - branch-dependent conditional two-qubit gates, - trajectory-batched energy estimation inside a gradient-based VQE loop.
passing_criteria: `len(energy_history) == 100`
`final_trajectory_energies.shape == (64,)`
the final trajectory-averaged energy is lower than the initial trajectory-averaged energy
the total energy improvement is at least `minimum_improvement = 0.3`
the final trajectory-averaged energy is at most `target_final_energy = -8.3`
all returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: The average energy improves by at least 0.3, reaches at most -8.3, and returns 64 final trajectory energies.
tasks.representation: Trajectory batch with classical branch-dependent feedback
tasks.scaling_pressure: High — trajectory count multiplies circuit cost
tasks.title: 16-Qubit Measurement-Feedback VQE
tasks.workflow: Measurement-feedback VQE over fixed stochastic trajectories

cross_methods.method: Boundary-MPS sampling with explicit error control

tasks.differentiability_pressure: None — sampling fidelity is the evaluator target
tasks.dominant_workload: 8,192 samples from a shallow two-dimensional circuit
tasks.goal: Sample from a 49-qubit shallow two-dimensional circuit without constructing the full `2^49` statevector. The entangling graph is a 7 by 7 square grid, and the intended computation samples by contracting the corresponding tensor network directly rather than by reducing the problem to a one-dimensional MPS-friendly geometry.
passing_criteria: `samples.shape == (8192, 49)`.
Every sample entry is either `0` or `1`.
The maximum hidden single-site `Z_i` finite-sample error is at most `0.03`.
The maximum hidden `Z`-string finite-sample error is at most `0.05`.
The mean hidden `Z`-string finite-sample error is at most `0.015`.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Returned samples meet shape/binary checks and hidden Z-string error tolerances.
tasks.scaling_pressure: Extreme — a 2^49 statevector and 1D reduction are disallowed
tasks.title: 7x7 Mixed-Axis Grid Tensor-Network Sampling

cross_methods.method: Parameter-shift or adjoint gradients on reduced circuits

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — every restart optimizes local expectations
tasks.dominant_workload: 20,000 restart-step updates on two irregular local observables
tasks.goal: Optimize two local Pauli observables in a large irregular but local variational circuit without constructing the full `2^512` statevector. The task is designed to test whether a framework can exploit finite causal cones for local measurements when the circuit is no longer a regular brickwork pattern.
passing_criteria: `observable_history.shape == (n_restarts, max_steps)`.
The initial and final objective arrays derived from `observable_history` both have shape `(n_restarts,)`.
The mean final local objective is larger than the mean initial local objective.
The best final local objective is at least `success_threshold`.
The final-objective variance recomputed by the evaluator is finite and non-negative.
All returned values are NumPy arrays or NumPy-compatible scalars.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Mean objective improves and the best final local objective reaches at least 1.0.
tasks.representation: Backward causal cones of 15 and 18 qubits
tasks.scaling_pressure: Extreme globally, compact after correct cone extraction
tasks.title: Random Local Light-Cone Optimization

tasks.dominant_workload: 200 updates with a high-arity diagonal operation
tasks.goal: Optimize a variational state whose ansatz contains a fixed 18-qubit controlled-Z gate acting on non-adjacent qubits. The task tests whether a framework can express and differentiate a large high-arity diagonal gate directly, without materializing a dense `2^18 x 2^18` matrix or decomposing the gate into a long sequence of small controlled gates.
passing_criteria: `energy_history.shape == (max_steps,)`.
`final_parameters.shape == (n_layers, n_qubits, 3)`.
The evaluator-computed largest ansatz gate size is `18`.
The final energy density is at least `minimum_energy_improvement` lower than the initial energy density.
The returned history is finite.
The final energy density is not below the exact ground-state energy density beyond `exact_lower_bound_tolerance`.

The final energy-density gap relative to the exact reference is at most `maximum_energy_density_gap`. This threshold is intentionally loose because the benchmark is about expressing and optimizing through the large `CMZ` hyperedge, not about solving the TFIM ground state to high precision.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Energy improves and finishes within 0.25 density units of the sparse exact reference.
tasks.representation: Matrix-free state update or structured diagonal tensor
tasks.scaling_pressure: Extreme — a dense 2^18 × 2^18 gate is forbidden
tasks.title: 22-Qubit VQE With an 18-Qubit Controlled-Z Hyperedge

tasks.differentiability_pressure: High — qutrit rotations and two-site exponentials are trained
tasks.dominant_workload: 500 updates of 290 parameters plus three nonlocal correlators
tasks.goal: Find a low-energy variational state for an open spin-1 chain in the Haldane phase and verify that the optimized state reproduces the expected nonlocal string order. The task is not only to lower the energy, but to produce a physically consistent final state whose hidden antiferromagnetic order can be checked from fixed string correlators.
passing_criteria: `energy_density_history.shape == (max_steps,)`.
`final_string_orders.shape == (3,)`.
The final energy density is at least `minimum_energy_improvement` lower than the initial energy density.
The returned arrays contain finite values.
The final energy density is no more than `maximum_energy_density_gap` above the exact ground-state density.
The mean absolute error of the three checked string correlators is at most `maximum_string_order_mae = 0.12`.
tasks.primary_success_criterion: Energy is close to exact and the three string correlators have mean absolute error at most 0.12.
tasks.scaling_pressure: High — Hilbert dimension is 3^12 rather than 2^12
tasks.title: Spin-1 Haldane-Chain VQE With String-Order Verification
tasks.workflow: Spin-1 Haldane-chain VQE with string-order verification
